acv.quote: About a hundred and forty K a year.

data.reason: Ines, the new CFO, signed after Wen priced her team's hand-matching of deposits using her own statements. Dana first pitched the ordering portal, which Ines said wasn't her problem.

trigger.action: Lead with a slow month-end close, not the ordering portal.
trigger.why: Ines's first close took nine days, partly from hand-matching deposits. The portal pitch cost Dana a month.
trigger.quote: her first month-end close took nine days.

decider.action: Open with closing the books faster, written for the CFO.
decider.why: Ines read only the first page of the portal proposal and set it aside for three weeks.
decider.quote: she read the first page and said it wasn't her problem.

competitor.action: Answer 'who helps me' with a named contact, not rates.
competitor.why: Ines's bank only offered a rate review, then she asked us for a named contact. Dana never saw Fiserv's pitch.
competitor.quote: I didn't ask about my rates.

message.action: Replace the global growth opener with payout-to-transaction matching.
message.why: The global deck got silence from Paul. Ines interrupted Wen's payout matching demo to see it again.
message.quote: Ines actually stopped him and said, 'go back.'

proof.action: Add a wholesale distributor customer story.
proof.why: Ines asked twice to talk to another distributor and brushed off the retail case study Dana sent.
proof.quote: this is a company that sells sweaters.

words.action: Say 'where my money is' and 'deposits', not 'infrastructure'.
words.why: Ines never said 'payments' or 'infrastructure'. She talked about the deposits and where her money was.
words.quote: I just want to know where my money is.
